question: Which among the following Articles of the Indian Constitution deal with 'Right to Freedom of Religion'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 25-28**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 25-28** of the Indian Constitution deal with the '**Right to Freedom of Religion**'.
 
• These articles ensure that all individuals have the freedom to profess, practice, and propagate their religion.
 
• The provisions under these articles also protect religious practices and allow religious groups to manage their own affairs in matters of religion.
 
• Article 25 guarantees **freedom of conscience** and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion.
 
• Article 26 ensures the** freedom to manage religious affairs**.
 
• Article 27 provides **freedom from payment of taxes **for promotion of any particular religion.
 
• Article 28 allows **freedom from attending religious **instruction or worship in certain educational institutions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Right to Freedom of Religion** is a fundamental right under **Part III** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These rights are subject to public order, morality, and health, and to other provisions of Part III of the Constitution.
 
• The Constitution of India aims to maintain a balance between the freedom of religion and other fundamental rights to ensure harmony and peace in the society.
 
• India is a secular state, which means that the state treats all religions impartially and does not uphold any religion as the state religion.
 
• **The Constitution of India was adopted on 26th November 1949 and came into effect on 26th January 1950.**
 
• It is the longest written constitution of any country in the world and lays down the framework for political principles, government structure, and the rights and duties of citizens.
